From a prototype to a business

A working prototype raises new questions. Who will buy it? What will it cost to make and deliver? Engineers and managers answer those questions together as they prepare a product for the market.

Two degrees, four specialisations

The BBA is proposed as a three- or four-year degree. The MBA is designed as a two-year degree. Confirm duration and specialisations for your preferred campus with admissions.

AI for Business

Analyse business data, automate routine work and use the findings to make decisions.

Supply Chain and Operations Management

Plan how to source, make and move products in India and internationally.

AI for Marketing and Sales

Use AI to find customers and support decisions about branding, marketing and sales.

Entrepreneurship and New Ventures

Find customers, set a price, explore funding and plan how a venture can grow.

From first customer to factory order

Management students can join engineering teams to identify a first customer and prepare for a factory order. Company projects give students practice making business decisions within real constraints.

Where it leads

Explore work in business analysis, operations and supply chain, marketing and sales, or start a company of your own.

For those who want the detail

The programme applies business fundamentals to company projects and product work. Management and engineering teams use cost, customer and operations data to decide how to bring a product to market.

Explore the founder path

Common questions

Which degree should I explore?

The BBA is an undergraduate business degree. The MBA is a postgraduate business degree. Ask admissions which entry routes apply to you.

Can BBA and MBA students choose the same specialisations?

The programme proposes the same four specialisations for both degrees. Confirm availability for your preferred campus with admissions.

Find the right business programme for you.

Compare the BBA and MBA routes with an adviser, and ask how each specialisation connects to company projects.
